components.label: Chunk producer
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Push coordinator
components.responsibility: Admit finite chunk work, execute bounded GPU batches and retain separate per-subscriber outstanding identities until acknowledged.

components.label: GPU batch queue
components.responsibility: submit() only tries to enqueue by chunk identity and answers queued, duplicate or rejected immediately; it never awaits GPU completion, so a burst fills the finite queue and the overflow is rejected visibly.

components.label: Synthetic batch worker
components.responsibility: One batch worker takes up to maxBatch queued chunks, or what arrived within the batch window, per modeled GPU call and records compute receipts by chunk ID before fan-out. Batching speed is a parameter, not measured hardware proof.

components.label: Subscriber ACK slots
components.responsibility: Track outstanding chunk IDs per subscriber/session with a fixed window; full subscribers receive a visible refusal or disconnection.

components.label: Coalescing CDN fill
components.responsibility: Maintain immutable content-key cache and single in-flight promise per key; bound distinct fill concurrency and waiter count.

components.label: Session ACK reducer
components.responsibility: Verify subscriber, session epoch and outstanding chunk ID; delete once. Unknown or duplicate ACKs change no occupancy.

components.label: Slow-session policy
components.responsibility: Expire or disconnect a session under declared deadline, release its local slots and retain explicit undelivered IDs; do not count them as acknowledged.

components.label: Conservation ledger
components.responsibility: For every submitted chunk and subscriber record delivered/ACKed/rejected/unfinished outcome; separate compute totals from fan-out totals.

components.label: Chunk producer
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Manifest publisher
components.responsibility: Compute finite immutable chunks once, publish versioned manifests with explicit gaps, and let each subscriber pull at its own rate through the CDN.

components.label: Bounded batch admission
components.responsibility: Admit source chunks into a finite deduplicated batch queue independent of subscriber demand. A repeated chunk ID returns its existing outcome; a chunk refused because the queue is full is published as an explicit rejected gap in the next manifest version.

components.label: GPU chunk writer
components.responsibility: Finish modeled batch output, hash bytes and store immutable chunk before publishing its manifest entry.

components.label: Immutable chunk spool
components.responsibility: Store immutable bytes by content key with one reference per manifest entry and one per in-flight read pin; pruning below the retained floor drops references and deletes bytes only when none remain, so a key shared with a retained chunk survives.

components.label: Versioned manifest
components.responsibility: Each commit, rejection gap or floor change publishes a new immutable version holding sorted entries, explicit gaps and the retained floor; readers take one version and old versions are never edited.

components.label: Subscriber pull cursor
components.responsibility: Subscriber requests next identity with bounded concurrency and advances after its own successful receipt or an explicit gap; the publisher keeps no per-subscriber slot or push wait.

components.label: Coalesced CDN reader
components.responsibility: In one step under the manifest lock, check the floor and pin the entry's content key; then coalesce identical misses, cap fills and waiters, verify the payload hash and unpin. Waiter cancellation stays independent.

components.label: Retention reset
components.responsibility: Return 410 with current floor and manifest version; require an explicit skip/reset that records the skipped range, or an archived recovery source, rather than claiming continuous delivery.

response.duplicate: true when the chunk ID was already admitted; state is its existing outcome

response.nextRequest: chunk ID, gap step or wait

requirements.text: Bound GPU batch queue, per-subscriber delivery state and cache-fill work; retain explicit rejected and unfinished chunks.
Track per-subscriber delivery progress separately from compute completion; a slow subscriber cannot silently consume unbounded memory.
Coalesce concurrent same-chunk CDN misses; define cancellation, retry identity and retained-history expiry.

problem.scope: Authored bounded streaming study of the catalogue scenario: synthetic finite video chunks, GPU batch work, a coalescing CDN cache and one slow consumer. The push approach holds acknowledged per-subscriber fan-out slots; the pull approach replaces them with subscriber-owned cursors over immutable, retention-bounded manifest versions and holds no per-subscriber slot. No codec, player, real GPU speedup, production sizing or infinite-stream claim.
problem.studyLabel: Finite streaming burst with a slow subscriber

evidence.testName: batch-08 streaming push: batch admission and ACK windows

acceptanceCases.given: Two subscribers with a window of one each; the slow one withholds its ACK.
acceptanceCases.then: The fast subscriber progresses; the slow one holds at most one outstanding chunk and its second chunk is recorded rejected-slow; disconnect records the unacknowledged chunk; stale-session and duplicate ACKs free nothing.
acceptanceCases.when: Send two chunks, ACK the fast subscriber, disconnect and reconnect the slow one, then replay its old-session ACK and a duplicate ACK.

evidence.testName: batch-08 streaming push: batch admission and ACK windows

acceptanceCases.given: A batch queue of capacity 4 with maxBatch 3 and a producer burst of 10 chunks while the worker is busy.
acceptanceCases.then: Chunks 0-3 are queued and 4-9 are recorded rejected-compute at submission; the worker computes [0,1,2] then [3] in two GPU calls; resubmitting chunk 0 is a duplicate, not new work.
acceptanceCases.when: Submit the burst, then run the batch worker until the queue is empty.

evidence.testName: batch-08 streaming: coalesced fill and cancellation

acceptanceCases.given: Two simultaneous cache misses for the same immutable chunk.
acceptanceCases.then: One fill executes; the live waiter receives the bytes; the canceled waiter receives no completion; a failed fill clears its in-flight entry so an explicit retry succeeds.
acceptanceCases.when: Start both fills, cancel one waiter, complete the fill, then fail and retry a different key.

guarantees: The queue bound applies to producer bursts; GPU work is batched; per-session occupancy is bounded; ACK and compute completion are not conflated.

stages.explanation: Admit finite chunk work, execute bounded GPU batches and retain separate per-subscriber outstanding identities until acknowledged. GPU completion and each subscriber ACK are separate states. [Presence information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence_information) describes a recently observed connection or activity. It is time-bounded evidence, not proof that a person or device will remain reachable after the observation.

stages.explanation: submit() only tries to enqueue by chunk identity and answers queued, duplicate or rejected immediately; it never awaits GPU completion, so a burst fills the finite queue and the overflow is rejected visibly. Every submitted chunk is queued, a duplicate, or recorded rejected at submission; rejection is never reported as completed work. [A queue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queue_%28abstract_data_type%29) separates accepting work from completing it.
invariants: Every submitted chunk is queued, a duplicate, or recorded rejected at submission; rejection is never reported as completed work.

stages.reason: submit() only tries to enqueue by chunk identity and answers queued, duplicate or rejected immediately; it never awaits GPU completion, so a burst fills the finite queue and the overflow is rejected visibly.
stages.title: Bound pending compute

stages.explanation: One batch worker takes up to maxBatch queued chunks, or what arrived within the batch window, per modeled GPU call and records compute receipts by chunk ID before fan-out. Batching speed is a parameter, not measured hardware proof. One GPU call covers at most maxBatch chunks, and each chunk ID is computed once with immutable output bytes. [Data ingestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integration) moves source records into a usable destination.

stages.explanation: Track outstanding chunk IDs per subscriber/session with a fixed window; full subscribers receive a visible refusal or disconnection. No subscriber holds more than its configured window. [Stream processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream_processing) updates results as events arrive. Arrival order may differ from event time, so late-data rules and bounded retained state are part of the result definition.
invariants: No subscriber holds more than its configured window.
stages.question: Why should one slow subscriber not block all recipients?
stages.reason: Track outstanding chunk IDs per subscriber/session with a fixed window; full subscribers receive a visible refusal or disconnection.
stages.title: Allocate independent windows

stages.explanation: Maintain immutable content-key cache and single in-flight promise per key; bound distinct fill concurrency and waiter count. A fill failure clears the in-flight entry so a later explicit retry may proceed. [A cache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_replacement_policies) keeps reusable results in limited memory. Eviction controls space, while ownership and invalidation rules determine whether a returned value is still safe to use.
invariants: A fill failure clears the in-flight entry so a later explicit retry may proceed.
stages.question: Can simultaneous subscribers trigger duplicate origin work?
stages.reason: Maintain immutable content-key cache and single in-flight promise per key; bound distinct fill concurrency and waiter count.
stages.title: Share a cache miss

stages.explanation: Verify subscriber, session epoch and outstanding chunk ID; delete once. Unknown or duplicate ACKs change no occupancy. An old session cannot free a new-session outstanding chunk. [Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect. Stable request identities let a retry recover an existing outcome instead of creating another change.
invariants: An old session cannot free a new-session outstanding chunk.
stages.question: What if old ACKs arrive after reconnect?
stages.reason: Verify subscriber, session epoch and outstanding chunk ID; delete once. Unknown or duplicate ACKs change no occupancy.
stages.title: Release only a matching slot

stages.explanation: Expire or disconnect a session under declared deadline, release its local slots and retain explicit undelivered IDs; do not count them as acknowledged. Resource reclamation is not delivery success. [Time to live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_to_live) defines when a value or right stops being valid. Expiration must be checked at the point of use, even when background cleanup runs later.
invariants: Resource reclamation is not delivery success.
stages.question: What if ACK never arrives?
stages.reason: Expire or disconnect a session under declared deadline, release its local slots and retain explicit undelivered IDs; do not count them as acknowledged.
stages.title: Terminate held resources

stages.explanation: For every submitted chunk and subscriber record delivered/ACKed/rejected/unfinished outcome; separate compute totals from fan-out totals. The finite input ledger balances without inventing completion. [Publish–subscribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publish%E2%80%93subscribe_pattern) separates producing an update from distributing it to interested consumers. Delivery cost shifts depending on whether work is performed when writing or when someone reads. Consider this case: Two subscribers with a window of one each; the slow one withholds its ACK.
invariants: The finite input ledger balances without inventing completion.
stages.question: Can rejected chunks disappear from the result?
stages.reason: For every submitted chunk and subscriber record delivered/ACKed/rejected/unfinished outcome; separate compute totals from fan-out totals.

Reject/drop policy must be visible; a slow subscriber cannot be promised lossless infinite retention.

evidence.testName: batch-08 streaming pull: manifest gaps, retention floor and pinned reads

acceptanceCases.given: A queue bound of two: chunks 0 and 1 admitted, chunk 2 refused, then duplicate submissions of 0 and 2.
acceptanceCases.then: The refusal is published as a gap in its own manifest version; duplicates return their existing outcome instead of a new rejection; the cursor receives 0 and 1, steps over gap 2 and then waits; the version holding the gap is unchanged by later commits.
acceptanceCases.when: Commit 0 and 1, then walk a cursor from 0.

evidence.testName: batch-08 streaming pull: manifest gaps, retention floor and pinned reads

acceptanceCases.given: Five committed chunks where 0 and 4 have identical bytes, and a read of chunk 1 already past its floor check.
acceptanceCases.then: The in-flight read still returns chunk 1's bytes, which are deleted only after it unpins; the shared key survives for chunk 4; the repeat request gets 410 with floor 3; reset records the skipped range [1,3); chunks 3 and 4 read normally.
acceptanceCases.when: Raise the floor to 3, finish the read, request chunk 1 again, reset the cursor, then read 3 and 4.

acceptanceCases.given: Two simultaneous cache misses for the same immutable chunk.
acceptanceCases.then: One fill executes; the live waiter receives the bytes; the canceled waiter receives no completion; a failed fill clears its in-flight entry so an explicit retry succeeds.
acceptanceCases.when: Start both fills, cancel one waiter, complete the fill, then fail and retry a different key.

guarantees: Pull demand is independent; rejected chunks are explicit gaps; retained bytes are reference-counted and pinned across reads; expiration is explicit.

solutions.chooseWhen: Consumers may lag independently and storage retention can absorb a bounded burst.

stages.explanation: Compute finite immutable chunks once, publish versioned manifests with explicit gaps, and let each subscriber pull at its own rate through the CDN. Each subscriber requests the next chunk only when it is ready; the publisher holds no ACK slot. [A content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) serves reusable content near viewers. Cache keys, freshness rules, and origin fallback determine whether that improves latency without serving the wrong version.
invariants: Each subscriber requests the next chunk only when it is ready; the publisher holds no ACK slot.

stages.explanation: Admit source chunks into a finite deduplicated batch queue independent of subscriber demand. A repeated chunk ID returns its existing outcome; a chunk refused because the queue is full is published as an explicit rejected gap in the next manifest version. Repeated submissions never schedule duplicate computation and are never recorded as rejections. [A queue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queue_%28abstract_data_type%29) separates accepting work from completing it.
invariants: Repeated submissions never schedule duplicate computation and are never recorded as rejections.

stages.explanation: Finish modeled batch output, hash bytes and store immutable chunk before publishing its manifest entry. No advertised entry points to an uncommitted output. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version. Consider this case: A queue bound of two: chunks 0 and 1 admitted, chunk 2 refused, then duplicate submissions of 0 and 2.

stages.reason: Finish modeled batch output, hash bytes and store immutable chunk before publishing its manifest entry.

stages.explanation: Store immutable bytes by content key with one reference per manifest entry and one per in-flight read pin; pruning below the retained floor drops references and deletes bytes only when none remain, so a key shared with a retained chunk survives. A pruned entry returns expired, never a different chunk, and bytes still referenced or pinned are never deleted. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers.
invariants: A pruned entry returns expired, never a different chunk, and bytes still referenced or pinned are never deleted.

stages.title: Retain a finite replay window

stages.explanation: Each commit, rejection gap or floor change publishes a new immutable version holding sorted entries, explicit gaps and the retained floor; readers take one version and old versions are never edited. A higher manifest version never changes old content hashes, and every rejected chunk appears as a gap a cursor can step over. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure.
invariants: A higher manifest version never changes old content hashes, and every rejected chunk appears as a gap a cursor can step over.

stages.explanation: Subscriber requests next identity with bounded concurrency and advances after its own successful receipt or an explicit gap; the publisher keeps no per-subscriber slot or push wait. A slow cursor allocates no publisher-side state; retained bytes are bounded by the spool budget, not by cursor lag. [Presence information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence_information) describes a recently observed connection or activity. It is time-bounded evidence, not proof that a person or device will remain reachable after the observation.
invariants: A slow cursor allocates no publisher-side state; retained bytes are bounded by the spool budget, not by cursor lag.

stages.explanation: In one step under the manifest lock, check the floor and pin the entry's content key; then coalesce identical misses, cap fills and waiters, verify the payload hash and unpin. Waiter cancellation stays independent. A floor advance during a read cannot delete the bytes that read pinned, and canceling one waiter does not cancel a fill others still need. [A condition variable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condition_variable) lets a thread sleep until shared state may have changed.
invariants: A floor advance during a read cannot delete the bytes that read pinned, and canceling one waiter does not cancel a fill others still need.

stages.reason: In one step under the manifest lock, check the floor and pin the entry's content key; then coalesce identical misses, cap fills and waiters, verify the payload hash and unpin. Waiter cancellation stays independent.

Retention loss remains a visible gap in finite-stream accounting. [A content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) serves reusable content near viewers. Cache keys, freshness rules, and origin fallback determine whether that improves latency without serving the wrong version.
invariants: Retention loss remains a visible gap in finite-stream accounting.
